informal_statement: If p is prime and a is an integer coprime to p, then a^(p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p).
lean4_signature: theorem ZMod.pow_card_sub_one_eq_one {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {a : ZMod p} (ha : a ≠ 0) : a ^ (p - 1) = 1

informal_statement: If a prime p divides the product ab of two integers a and b, then p divides a or p divides b.
lean4_signature: theorem Nat.Prime.dvd_mul {p a b : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (h : p ∣ a * b) : p ∣ a ∨ p ∣ b

informal_statement: A natural number n > 1 is prime if and only if (n-1)! ≡ -1 (mod n).
lean4_signature: theorem ZMod.wilsons_lemma (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : ((Nat.factorial (p - 1) : ZMod p)) = -1

concept_name: Euclid's Theorem on Infinitude of Primes
informal_statement: There are infinitely many prime numbers; for every natural number n, there exists a prime p greater than n.
lean4_signature: theorem Nat.exists_infinite_primes (n : ℕ) : ∃ p, p ≥ n ∧ Nat.Prime p

informal_statement: For any integers a and b with greatest common divisor d = gcd(a,b), there exist integers x and y such that ax + by = d.
lean4_signature: theorem Nat.gcd_eq_gcd_ab (a b : ℕ) : ∃ (x y : ℤ), (x * (a : ℤ) + y * (b : ℤ) : ℤ) = Nat.gcd a b

informal_statement: If m and n are coprime positive integers, then for any integers a and b there exists a unique solution x modulo mn satisfying x ≡ a (mod m) and x ≡ b (mod n).
lean4_signature: theorem ZMod.chineseRemainder {m n : ℕ} (h : Nat.Coprime m n) : ZMod (m * n) ≃+* ZMod m × ZMod n

informal_statement: If n is a positive integer and a is an integer coprime to n, then a^φ(n) ≡ 1 (mod n), where φ is Euler's totient function.
lean4_signature: theorem Nat.modeq_pow_totient {a n : ℕ} (h : Nat.Coprime a n) : a ^ Nat.totient n ≡ 1 [MOD n]

concept_name: Divisibility of Product of Consecutive Integers
informal_statement: The product of k consecutive integers is divisible by k! (k factorial).
lean4_signature: theorem Nat.factorial_dvd_descFactorial (n k : ℕ) : Nat.factorial k ∣ Nat.descFactorial n k

informal_statement: Every integer greater than 1 either is a prime itself or can be represented as the product of prime numbers, and this representation is unique up to order.

concept_name: Multiplicativity of Sum of Divisors Function
informal_statement: The sum of divisors function σ(n) is multiplicative: if m and n are coprime integers, then σ(mn) = σ(m)σ(n).
lean4_signature: theorem Nat.sum_divisors_mul {m n : ℕ} (h : Nat.Coprime m n) : Nat.sigma (m * n) = Nat.sigma m * Nat.sigma n
